### 🟢 Approval recommended The change is confined to test code and its assertions exactly match the verified production port-check messages, statuses, and single `listen` call path, eliminating the prior port-selection race without risk to runtime behavior. **No open issues** 🎉
What changed in this PR This PR makes the `doctor` port-availability tests in `packages/server/tests/doctor.test.js` deterministic. Previously the tests used fixed high ports (`59123`/`59124`) and assumed availability, which is race-prone. The revised tests either hold a real OS-selected loopback listener open to reliably trigger the "occupied port" warning, or mock `Server.prototype.listen` to force a genuine successful bind on an OS-assigned port while still asserting the requested port/host were forwarded. I verified the assertions exactly match `runDoctorChecks`/`checkPortAvailable` in `packages/server/src/doctor.js` (messages `${port} is available` / `${port} is in use (server may already be running)` and statuses `pass`/`warn`). I also confirmed `doctor.js` calls `.listen` exactly once (only in `checkPortAvailable`), so the global `Server.prototype.listen` mock in the bind-success test intercepts only that single call, making `assert.deepEqual(calls, [[port, '127.0.0.1']])` sound. The `t.mock.method`/`t.after`/`async (t)` patterns are consistent with the existing server test suite. **Changes:** - Added an `occupyPort(t)` helper that keeps an OS-selected loopback listener open until test teardown, removing the select-then-check availability race. - Rewrote the custom-port test to assert the exact occupied-port warning message and `warn` status. - Added a bind-success test that mocks `Server.prototype.listen` to redirect to port 0, preserving a real successful bind without a release/rebind race, and verifies the forwarded port and host. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | packages/​server/​tests/​doctor.test.js | Introduces `occupyPort` helper and rewrites three port-check tests to be deterministic; assertions verified against `doctor.js` message/status output. |
